properties.name: A session reports the work it did BY HAND that reflow2 already serves — the negative space, which is the only signal that tells an unfindable tool from an unwanted one
properties.statement:
Promoted to intent from `dec:idea-can-reflow2-see-the-work-a-session-did-by-hand` on Anthony's word, 2026-08-26. That node is the OPEN QUESTION with its four options and their counter-arguments; this is the INTENT chosen out of it. Both are kept, per the brainstorm discipline: the road taken is recorded on the question, and the question keeps the roads not taken.

Every measurement reflow2 has of its own adoption looks at what a session DID with it: `surface_usage.py` counts calls, `cap:skill-loads-are-counted` counts loads, `dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage` asks where the log lives. All are blind to the same thing — **the work a session performed by hand that reflow2 already serves.**

THAT NEGATIVE SPACE IS A STRONGER SIGNAL THAN ABSENCE-OF-A-CALL, BECAUSE IT CARRIES INTENT. `dec:bl-155` measured 40 of 132 tools never called and states outright that it *"cannot tell unused from unreachable"*, listing three explanations it has no way to separate: genuinely young, no use case yet, or findable by nobody. **Hand-rolled work discriminates between them.** A session that wrote a script to do X proves somebody wanted X, at a moment, badly enough to build it — which a zero in a usage table can never show.

MEASURED THREE TIMES ACROSS FIVE WEEKS, AND TWICE IT FOUND THE SESSION'S CENTRAL RESULT:
- **2026-08-26** — comparing the allocation layer against the artifact layer (212 capabilities: 59 agree, 23 disagree, 130 no evidence) was done with hand-written Python over the export. **No reflow2 tool does it**: `reconcile_artifacts` compares design against DISK, `compare_designs` compares design against DESIGN, and neither compares two layers of ONE design. Here the signal names a MISSING tool.
- **2026-08-20** — *"does my declared decomposition match the real coupling?"* — again hand-written, again the session's finding.
- **The v0.19.0–v0.31.0 release cuts** — a JSON-RPC export driver written and rewritten until it was promoted into `tools/`. The same signal, acted on late.

⭐ THE SIGNAL PRODUCES TWO DIFFERENT DIAGNOSES AND DOES NOT NEED TO TELL THEM APART: sometimes the tool is MISSING, sometimes it exists and was not FOUND. A human reading the list can, and either answer is worth having.

WHAT MUST BE TRUE OF ANY IMPLEMENTATION:
- It must respect `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` — the SHAPE of the work, never its content. A script's source is design content and must not travel.
- It must not depend on the agent having noticed the tool existed, or it measures the same blind spot it is trying to see. **This is the standing objection to the chosen form and it is NOT resolved by choosing it.**

📌 THE FORM CHOSEN, deliberately the cheapest: **ask the agent at session end what it did by hand that reflow2 should have done.** Both prior findings surfaced exactly that way — an agent noticing and saying so, unprompted — so the mechanism is known to work at least sometimes, and a transcript-side detector is a larger build with a privacy posture reflow2 has never taken. If asking proves unreliable the detector remains available; starting with it would have been building before measuring, which is the over-engineering this project watches for by name.
